questions.q: What redundancy does ZeRO target that plain data parallelism has?
options: Redundant copies of the training dataset on disk
Full, replicated copies of optimizer state, gradients, and parameters on every GPU, even though each replica only needs its own slice at any given moment
Redundant logging of training metrics
Duplicate forward passes on the same data
questions.explain: In plain DDP, every GPU stores a complete copy of parameters, gradients, and optimizer state. ZeRO shards these instead of replicating them, since no GPU needs the full copy of all of it simultaneously.

questions.q: What distinguishes ZeRO stage 1 from stage 2 from stage 3?
options: They are three unrelated optimizers with no shared design
Stage 1 shards optimizer state; stage 2 additionally shards gradients; stage 3 additionally shards parameters themselves, so no GPU holds the full model at rest
Each stage uses a different learning rate schedule
Stage 3 disables gradient computation entirely
questions.explain: ZeRO's three stages progressively shard more memory-heavy state: stage 1 optimizer state only, stage 2 adds gradients, and stage 3 adds parameters, trading more communication for more memory savings at each step.

questions.q: Under ZeRO stage 3 or FSDP's FULL_SHARD strategy, how are a layer's full parameters made available for computation?
options: They are never fully reconstructed -- computation happens directly on shards
An all-gather reconstructs the full layer weights from shards right before they're needed for forward or backward computation, then frees them immediately afterward
The parameters are permanently copied to every GPU at the start of training
They are read from disk on every forward pass
questions.explain: Stage 3 / FULL_SHARD sharding reconstructs each shardable unit's parameters via an all-gather exactly when needed, then releases that memory right after, rather than keeping full copies resident.

questions.q: What is PyTorch's FullyShardedDataParallel (FSDP) relative to ZeRO?
options: A completely unrelated memory-saving technique with no overlap with ZeRO
PyTorch's native implementation of essentially the same sharding idea, with FULL_SHARD roughly equivalent to ZeRO stage 3
A tool only usable for inference, never training
A replacement for DistributedDataParallel that disables data parallelism entirely
questions.explain: FSDP implements the same core sharding idea as ZeRO as a native PyTorch API; its FULL_SHARD strategy is roughly equivalent to ZeRO stage 3, and SHARD_GRAD_OP is roughly equivalent to stage 2.

questions.q: What is the core trade-off when choosing a more aggressive ZeRO/FSDP sharding stage?
options: More aggressive stages always run strictly faster with no downside
More aggressive sharding reduces per-GPU memory usage but increases the volume of communication required during training
More aggressive stages eliminate the need for gradient synchronization entirely
More aggressive stages only affect inference, not training
questions.explain: Each more aggressive ZeRO/FSDP stage shards more state, which reduces per-GPU memory but requires more frequent communication (such as all-gathers) to reconstruct state on demand, making it a genuine trade-off rather than a free upgrade.
